questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en:
If I were in charge of the last project

I would have delegated a little more

than the project manager did

No error
options_hi:
If I were in charge of the last project

I would have delegated a little more

than the project manager did

No error
questions.solution_en:
Option A — replace “were” with “had been”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Third Conditional (Unreal Past Condition)

This sentence refers to:

  • a completed project in the past
  • a hypothetical situation contrary to fact

The correct conditional structure for unreal past situations is:

If + had been / had + V³ → would have + V³

💢 Application to the Given Question

“the last project”

  • Clearly refers to a finished past event
  • Hence, the condition must be located in the past unreal

“would have delegated”

  • Correct third-conditional result form
  • Already fixed in the past hypothetical frame

Therefore:

  • if I had been in charge ✅
  • if I were in charge ❌ (this form is for unreal present, not unreal past)

Since the result clause is already correct, the only error lies in Part A.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The workload assigned to the finance team this quarter
is very heavier than the previous quarter, leading
to increased stress and longer working hours.
options_hi: The workload assigned to the finance team this quarter
is very heavier than the previous quarter, leading
to increased stress and longer working hours.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “very heavier” with much heavier or far heavier.

Rule / Concept: Modification of Comparatives -

You cannot use “very” with comparative adjectives.

To intensify comparatives, use “much” or “far” instead of “very.”

SSC CGL often traps candidates by combining “very” with comparatives in long, complex sentences.

Application to the Given Question - Here, “heavier” is a comparative adjective. Using “very” is incorrect. The correct intensifiers for comparatives are “much” or “far”.

Corrected Sentence - The workload assigned to the finance team this quarter is much heavier (or far heavier) than the previous quarter, leading to increased stress and longer working hours.

More Examples for Clarity -

He is much taller than his brother.

The new system is far more efficient than the old one.

This road is much narrower than the highway.

Incorrect Usage -

She is very smarter than her classmates.

The project is very more complex than expected.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

Check the adjective: if it’s a comparative, never use “very”.

Intensify comparatives with much or far only.

questions.q_en:
Identify the type of the highlighted clause.

The teacher realized that several students had misunderstood the instructions completely.
questions.q_hi:
Identify the type of the highlighted clause.

The teacher realized that several students had misunderstood the instructions completely.
questions.solution_en:
Answer: C) Noun Clause

Explanation: A noun clause is a subordinate clause that functions as a noun in a sentence. It may act as a subject, object, or complement.

The highlighted clause:

“that several students had misunderstood the instructions completely” acts as the object of the verb “realized.”

realized what? → that several students had misunderstood the instructions completely

Therefore, it is a noun clause.

Why other options are incorrect:

A) An adjective clause describes a noun or pronoun.

B) An adverb clause modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb.

D) A coordinate clause is joined to another clause with coordinating conjunctions like and, but, or.

Techniques such as gene editing and synthetic biology offer unprecedented control over biological processes; however, critics caution that rapid innovation can [----1---] ethical scrutiny if commercial incentives dominate decision-making. Additionally, unequal access to biotechnological advances risks [---2---] existing global disparities in healthcare and food security. Public apprehension is further fueled when scientific communication remains [---3---], failing to clearly explain risks, benefits, and limitations. Experts therefore stress that responsible progress in biotechnology requires a [---4---] governance framework that aligns innovation with societal values.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [4] :

questions.q_en:
When Arvind accepted the managerial position at a declining textile firm, he was aware that the challenge extended far beyond falling profits. The company’s real ailment lay buried in its culture—an unspoken resistance to accountability that had slowly normalized mediocrity. Employees met deadlines just well enough to avoid reprimand, innovation was quietly discouraged under the guise of “practicality,” and senior leadership equated stability with stagnation. Arvind initially chose restraint over disruption, believing that trust must precede transformation. However, this cautious approach was soon misinterpreted as indecision, reinforcing the very complacency he intended to dismantle.

As months passed, subtle patterns emerged. Suggestions were applauded in meetings but ignored in execution, data was selectively presented to justify inaction, and failures were attributed to external forces rather than internal inefficiencies. Arvind realized that the organization did not lack talent; it lacked the discomfort necessary for growth. When he finally introduced performance-linked evaluations and transparent reporting mechanisms, resistance intensified. Critics accused him of eroding harmony and imposing corporate rigidity on a “family-like” workplace. Yet beneath these objections lay a deeper fear—the loss of anonymity in collective failure. The turning point came not through dramatic reform but through consistency. Arvind refused to reverse decisions despite mounting pressure, yet he also resisted authoritarian impulses. Over time, clarity replaced confusion. While some employees exited, others adapted, discovering that accountability, though unsettling, offered professional dignity. The firm did not transform overnight, nor did it achieve spectacular success. But it shed its illusion of comfort, replacing it with a fragile yet honest culture—one where progress was measured not by immediate results, but by the willingness to confront inconvenient truths.

What does the passage suggest was the company’s most fundamental problem?

📌Rule/Concept: Don’t use ‘as’ after these verbs:-

Make, Choose, Elect, Select, Anoint, appoint, Name, Call, Think, Consider etc.

Certain verbs (often called Object Complement verbs) directly link the object to its new designation or quality. When using verbs like Make, Name, Elect, Choose, Call, Appoint, or Crown, the word "as" should not be used.

Correct Structure: Subject + Verb + Object + Noun/Adjective.

Incorrect Structure: Subject + Verb + Object + AS + Noun/Adjective.

While we use "as" with verbs like Regard, Treat, Describe, or Portray, it is strictly prohibited with Make.

Structure: verb + object + (as ❌) + object complement.

The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

In accordance with the ethical guidelines of journalism, a reporter _________ verify the authenticity of a lead from at least two independent sources before publishing it.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

In accordance with the ethical guidelines of journalism, a reporter _________ verify the authenticity of a lead from at least two independent sources before publishing it.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (a).

Rule / Concept: Ought to (Moral Duty and Correctness)-

Ought to is a modal verb used to express a moral obligation, duty, or the "correct" thing to do according to a standard or ethical code. It is structurally unique among modals because it must be followed by the to-infinitive (to + V1). While 'should' also expresses duty, 'ought to' is preferred when referring to laws, regulations, or established social ethics.

Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the context is "ethical guidelines of journalism." This refers to a professional moral code. Since the blank is followed by the base form "verify," we need a modal.

  • Why not "Should"? While "should" is logically similar, in many competitive exams, when a sentence refers to "Ethical Guidelines," "Fundamental Duties," or "Constitutional Values," 'Ought to' is the more precise choice to reflect a formal moral obligation.

More Examples for Clarity

  1. You ought to respect your elders. (Moral Duty) ✔

  2. We ought to follow the traffic rules for everyone's safety. (Social Obligation) ✔

  3. This film ought to win an award for its screenplay. (Strong Desirability) ✔

Incorrect Usage

  1. We should to help the poor. (Never use 'to' with should) ❌

  2. You ought respect your parents. (Missing 'to') ❌

questions.solution_en:
Replace “Parliament” with “the Parliament”.

Rule / Concept: Use of 'The' with Holy Books, Newspapers, and Statutory Bodies -

The definite article 'the' is used before the names of holy books (e.g., the Geeta), newspapers (e.g., the Times of India), and statutory or constitutional bodies (e.g., the Parliament, the Judiciary).

However, 'the' is not used before holy books when the author's name precedes them (e.g., Valmiki’s Ramayana).

Corrected Sentence- The speaker of Lok Sabha emphasized that the Parliament represents the collective will and aspirations of the people of India.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips- Just as we use 'the' for the press (The Hindu) and the wings of government (The Executive), always ensure these formal titles are treated as specific nouns.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The software update unexpectedly __________ several critical errors during testing.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The software update unexpectedly __________ several critical errors during testing.
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (3).

English Explanation: “Throw up” can mean to produce something unexpectedly (such as problems, questions, or difficulties). In the sentence, the software update unexpectedly produced several critical errors during testing. Therefore, “threw up” correctly conveys the idea of something generating or causing unexpected issues. “Throw off” means to confuse or distract someone. “Throw out” means to discard or reject something. “Throw in” means to include something extra, often as a bonus. Since the context is about unexpected errors being generated, “throw up” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Throw off (भ्रमित करना / ध्यान भटकाना)

Example: His sudden question threw me off during the presentation. (उसके अचानक प्रश्न ने प्रस्तुति के दौरान मुझे भ्रमित कर दिया।)

2. Throw out (फेंक देना / अस्वीकार करना)

Example: The committee threw out the proposal. (समिति ने प्रस्ताव को खारिज कर दिया।)

3. Throw up (उत्पन्न करना / अचानक सामने लाना)

Example 1: The discussion threw up several important questions. (चर्चा के दौरान कई महत्वपूर्ण प्रश्न सामने आए।)

4. Throw in (अतिरिक्त रूप से शामिल करना)

Example: The seller threw in a free accessory with the phone. (विक्रेता ने फोन के साथ एक मुफ्त एक्सेसरी भी शामिल कर दी।)

Additionally, unequal access to biotechnological advances risks [---2---] existing global disparities in healthcare and food security. Public apprehension is further fueled when scientific communication remains [---3---], failing to clearly explain risks, benefits, and limitations. Experts therefore stress that responsible progress in biotechnology requires a [---4---] governance framework that aligns innovation with societal values.
